headline: Monday night: Bills @ Rams on MNF, ALCS Game 1 (Guardians @ Rays), and Wild-Golden Knights. NLCS Game 2 and Senators-Devils have already started, and there's no WNBA, golf or soccer tonight.
notes: Everything here starts around 5:00 PM PT. Bet before first pitch / puck drop / kickoff.
No game totals again. They went 0-7 on the first two boards.
No bet is a lock. 'Confidence' runs 1–5, and nothing tonight is above a 3.
Odds move. Skip any pick whose price is past the 'playable to' number in its reasoning. Prices marked 'estimate' come from prediction-market percentages; check your book.

sections.label: Best of the Day
sections.slate: A short card: three bettable games tonight. These are the picks with the most support.

straight.reasoning: The line moved from Rams -3 to -3.5 even though about 79% of spread tickets are on Buffalo, which points to sharper money on LA. Buffalo is banged up: top pass rusher Ed Oliver and WR Josh Palmer are out, CB Christian Benford missed last week, and D.J. Moore is questionable. The Rams' run game ranks 8th in success rate and 2nd in adjusted line yards, and Buffalo is 31st at stopping handoffs. That lets LA control the clock and limit Josh Allen's possessions. The Rams also allow just 4.2 yards per play, 2nd in the NFL. Don't pay -4.

Drew Rasmussen gave up one hit over eight innings with 10 strikeouts against the Yankees in the ALDS, and he struck out 15 Guardians in 12 innings this season. Cleveland counters with Foster Griffin (3.38 ERA) and a bullpen taxed by its ALDS. Tampa Bay had five days of rest. The market has the Rays around 60%. Playable to -160 (price is an estimate).

parlay.title: Monday Night Favorites
parlay.reasoning: Two home favorites with clear matchup edges, combined into a plus-money ticket. Using the Rams moneyline instead of -3.5 means a Rams win by 1-3 still pays.

props.reasoning: He has 10+ strikeouts in each of his last two starts and struck out 15 Guardians in 12 innings this season. Six strikeouts is a modest bar for that form. Playable to -145.

Palmer is out and Moore is questionable, so Shakir should see extra targets. The Rams have allowed the 3rd-most yards to slot receivers and play zone at the 8th-highest rate, which is the coverage Shakir has beaten most over the last three seasons. Covers projects 51.5 yards. Price is an estimate from a 57% market probability.

props.pick: Jack Eichel OVER 2.5 shots on goal
props.reasoning: Vegas averages 33 shots a game and Eichel leads the team with 12 points. Dimers' model puts him at 66.5% to get 3+ shots, about 6 points above what -155 implies. Playable to -165.

parlay.title: Rasmussen Dominates (SGP)
parlay.reasoning: If Rasmussen is piling up strikeouts, Tampa Bay is probably winning — the two go together. Books price that correlation in, so expect less than the multiplied odds.

props.reasoning: 10+ strikeouts in each of his last two starts, and 15 strikeouts in 12 innings against Cleveland this season. Playable to -145.
Covers' pick for this game, against a back-end Cleveland starter (Foster Griffin) and a taxed bullpen. A single plus a run scored clears it. Price is an estimate.

sections.label: Football
sections.slate: Monday Night Football: Bills (3-1) @ Rams (2-2), SoFi Stadium, 5:15 PM PT.

straight.reasoning: The line moved through 3 to 3.5 even though 79% of spread tickets are on Buffalo. Buffalo is without Ed Oliver and Josh Palmer, CB Benford missed last week, and Moore is questionable. LA's run game (2nd in adjusted line yards) faces Buffalo's 31st-ranked run defense. The Rams allow 4.2 yards per play, 2nd in the league. The risk is Stafford's 6 interceptions in four games. Don't pay -4.

parlay.title: Rams Control the Game (SGP)
parlay.reasoning: With the Rams' other two tight ends hurt, Higbee is a steady short-yardage target in a ball-control game plan — the same game script that leads to a Rams win. Higbee's price is an estimate.

props.reasoning: Buffalo is short at receiver (Palmer out, Moore questionable). The Rams have allowed the 3rd-most yards to slot receivers and play a lot of zone, where Shakir has been Buffalo's best weapon. Covers projects 51.5 yards. Price is an estimate.

Higbee has 17 targets and 13 catches over the last two games, and Terrance Ferguson (IR) and Colby Parkinson (inactive) are out. Buffalo allows 5.4 catches a game to tight ends; Hunter Henry caught 5 against them last week. The projection sits right at 3, so it's a half unit. Price is an estimate.

sections.label: Hockey
sections.slate: Golden Knights @ Wild at 5:00 PM PT. Senators @ Devils starts at 4:00 PM PT, so only bet it if it hasn't started. Panthers-Sabres was an afternoon game.

parlay.title: Wild Top Line (SGP)
parlay.reasoning: Minnesota's top line played 4:30 more at 5-on-5 than any other line on Saturday and had 7 points in a 4-1 win. All three are on a power play converting 37.5% (2nd in the NHL), and Vegas has allowed a power-play goal in three of its last four. Covers rates the pair at 50% against a 43% market. Leg prices are estimates.

props.pick: Jack Eichel OVER 2.5 shots on goal
props.reasoning: Vegas generates 33 shots a game, and Eichel drives the offense with a team-high 12 points. Dimers' model gives him a 66.5% chance against about 61% implied. Playable to -165.

props.pick: William Karlsson OVER 1.5 shots on goal
props.reasoning: Dimers' model gives him a 70.3% chance against 63.6% implied — the biggest edge among the safer shot props. Two shots is a low bar for a top-six center on a 33-shot team. It's expensive, so a half unit.

Pinto has points in four of five games, plays 19+ minutes as the second-line center, and is getting more power-play time. Covers rates it at 55% against 45% in the market. This game starts at 4:00 PM PT, so skip it if it's already underway. Price is an estimate.
